paragraph: Canada had a population of approximately 41.6 million people in 2025, making it one of the world's most populous countries. Ontario had approximately 16.2 million residents, representing about 39% of Canada's population. Quebec had approximately 9.1 million people, while British Columbia had approximately 5.7 million. Canada's nominal GDP was approximately $2.32 trillion USD in 2025, with GDP per capita reaching approximately $55,698 USD.

India had an estimated population of approximately 1.464 billion people in 2025, while China had approximately 1.407 billion. The United States had approximately 341.8 million residents, making it the 3rd most populous country. India's nominal GDP was approximately $3.96 trillion USD in 2025, compared with China's $19.50 trillion USD. India's population was therefore more than 4 times larger than that of the United States.

Toronto is Canada's largest metropolitan area, with approximately 6.2 million residents recorded in the 2021 census. Montreal had approximately 4.29 million people, while Vancouver had approximately 2.64 million. Calgary's metropolitan population was approximately 1.48 million in 2021, and Ottawa-Gatineau had approximately 1.49 million. Together, these metropolitan areas account for a substantial portion of Canada's urban population.

Unit conversions are useful when comparing measurements from different systems. A distance of 15 km is equivalent to 9.32 miles, while 100 miles is approximately 160.93 km. If a vehicle travels at 100 km/h, its speed is approximately 62.14 mph. Similarly, a temperature of 25°C is equivalent to 77°F, using the formula °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32.

The United States had an estimated population of approximately 341.8 million in 2025, while California had approximately 39.5 million residents. Texas had approximately 31.7 million people, making it the 2nd most populous state. New York State had approximately 20 million residents, while Florida had approximately 23.8 million. The United States recorded a nominal GDP of approximately $30.77 trillion USD in 2025, the largest national economy in the world.

Population density helps explain how people are distributed across different geographical areas. Bangladesh had approximately 175.7 million residents in 2025 despite having a land area of approximately 148,460 km². Pakistan had approximately 255.2 million people, while Nigeria had approximately 237.5 million. By comparison, Brazil had approximately 212.8 million residents across an area of approximately 8.52 million km². These figures demonstrate how population size and geographical area can vary considerably between countries.

Cooking measurements frequently require conversions between metric and imperial units. One US cup holds approximately 236.59 mL, while 1 US tablespoon equals approximately 14.79 mL. A recipe requiring 500 g of flour needs approximately 1.10 pounds of flour. Additionally, 2 litres of water is equivalent to approximately 0.53 US gallons. These conversions help ensure accurate ingredient measurements when following international recipes.

Germany had approximately 83.5 million residents in 2025, while France had approximately 68.7 million and Italy had approximately 58.9 million. Germany's nominal GDP reached approximately $5.05 trillion USD in 2025, making it Europe's largest national economy. France recorded a nominal GDP of approximately $3.37 trillion USD, while Italy reached approximately $2.55 trillion USD. Germany's GDP per capita was approximately $60,496 USD, compared with approximately $49,000 USD in France.

Area and volume measurements are important when calculating the dimensions of buildings and rooms. A rectangular room measuring 5 m by 4 m has a floor area of 20 m². If its ceiling is 2.5 m high, its total internal volume is 50 m³. One square metre is equivalent to approximately 10.764 square feet, meaning that a 100 m² apartment has approximately 1,076.4 square feet of floor space. One cubic metre is also equivalent to 1,000 litres.

Australia had approximately 27 million residents in 2025, while its largest state, New South Wales, had approximately 8.5 million people. Victoria had approximately 7 million residents, and Queensland had approximately 5.7 million. Australia's nominal GDP was approximately $1.80 trillion USD in 2025, with annual GDP growth of approximately 2.1% according to World Bank data. Its population is concentrated primarily in major coastal cities such as Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth.
